# Decision register

The single list of decisions later work may rely on. It has one row per decision, taken from:
- the gate documents and RFCs of the first roadmap;
- the decision sections of the suite documents;
- the binding decisions both roadmaps carry forward.

A verdict a document states but this register does not list is evidence, not permission.

**The count at creation (2026-09-29):** 82 rows.
- **RATIFIED:** 78.
  - 4 reviewed by Carl;
  - 74 ratified by delegation under his standing instruction of 2026-09-29, which is not a review of the verdict.
- **PROPOSED:** 4.
- **DELEGATED, SUPERSEDED, REVERSED:** none.

Every row ratified by delegation is on Carl's ratification docket, which sits outside the repository beside the roadmaps. Each stays his to review, revise or reverse.

## How to use this register

- **Statuses.** A row has one of five:
  - **RATIFIED**: Carl has confirmed it, directly or by the delegation his standing instruction of 2026-09-29 gives. The row says which, when and where.
  - **DELEGATED**: decided on a recommendation while Carl was away, and not yet ratified in either way.
  - **SUPERSEDED**: replaced by a later decision, which the row names.
  - **REVERSED**: withdrawn. The row says by whom, when and why.
  - **PROPOSED**: a decision Roadmap II introduces, adopted when the prompts it names land.
- **Building on a row:**
  - a prompt may build on a **RATIFIED** row;
  - it may build on a **DELEGATED** row only if its Run condition says so, and it records the dependency in its PR;
  - it may never build on a **REVERSED** row.
- **Changing a status:** Carl edits the row, in a one-line commit that says why. A delegated ratification he reviews has its status (the fifth column) set to **RATIFIED**, and the sixth column ("Ratified where and how") begins "Reviewed by Carl, <date>" and keeps the old text after "was DELEGATED:"; a verdict he rejects becomes **REVERSED**, with the reason.
- **Adding decisions:** a new gate adds its rows when its decision document lands. tests/decisionRegister.test.js fails if any `*_GATE.md` or `*_RFC.md` has no row.
- **The Roadmap II prompts column** names the prompts that rely on the row, as the roadmap's run conditions do.

Angles are dimensionless but carried as angles, a magnitude scales only by a plain number, a unit not stated is refused, and a result has a registry unit, is dimensionless or says it has none. Uncertainty is first order for uncorrelated inputs through partial derivatives (a quantity used twice is differentiated once); an input with none gives a result with none, an interval is refused with a pointer to the bootstrap, and an aggregate sharing an input is not propagated. Arguments separate with `;` (and `,` in English) so Spanish decimals read through the shared reader. The module's own ceiling is 6,144 bytes gzipped for the language (measured 5,808) and 6,656 for the language with the question grader (measured 6,228), held by `tests/formula.test.js`. | **RATIFIED** | Recommended and taken on Carl's instruction to go with the recommendation, 2026-10-11; not yet reviewed; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-13 (all delegated rows) | Carl rejecting the grammar or asking for a different uncertainty rule | 100 |

It is a module of its own, imported only by lazy chunks (the Observatory's panels), so no sources-route request moved (figure 117 of 117, Studio 40 of 40, composer 29, Observatory 16) and no size ceiling moved; deferred 2033.1 of 2033.2 KB. Rule (cheap, in the architecture check): a module that exports `mount*` and calls `addEventListener` without importing the helper is reported unless it is in `tools/listener-helper-allowlist.json`; the record may only shrink (a module that adopts the helper must leave it). Every module-size ceiling is exact, so adopting the helper costs a module its few lines (an import, a scope, an `off()`): the fit panel took it line-neutral (one-line `destroy`), the other fifteen mounting modules are recorded and take it in the slice that makes room, which is why no ceiling was raised. Scopes live as long as their mount: a registration made on something a panel redraws (rows, parameter fields) stays a plain `addEventListener`, because a scope holds what it was given until `off()` and would keep every discarded control alive. The Composer and the Studio are single pages that wire once and rebuild their editors on elements the rebuild discards; neither mounts and unmounts a panel, so neither takes the helper, and the census proves twenty rebuilds of each add no listener. LEAK FOUND AND FIXED (5f20a3b4): the Observatory's fit panel put a `change` listener on its host (`#obsFitBody`) when mounted and never took it back; every language change re-mounts the panel at the same host, so each one left another, all running price() on every change in the fit form (40 across twenty cycles of two changes). `destroy()` now calls `off()`. Regression test: `e2e/lessonPerformance.spec.js` (Observatory cycle with a language change; 40 growth before the fix, 0 after; allowance 4). No other leak: the census on the Observatory's six panels, the Composer and the Studio shows 0 growth over twenty cycles once the fit panel is fixed. The census learned that a listener added with a signal is gone when the signal aborts. | **RATIFIED** | Decided on the recommendation under Carl's standing instruction, 2026-10-12; pending Carl's ratification; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-13 (all delegated rows) | Adopting the helper in all sixteen mounting modules now (raises sixteen exact ceilings); putting the helper in an existing module (every module's ceiling is exact and the pages share no module with the Observatory); a scope per panel for redrawn controls (retains them) | 107 |

| D-CANMOVE-01 | The grace period of `BlackHole.can_move` is 50 simulated units, the old 10 wall-clock seconds at 1x speed, counted in integrated simulated time (D-R7-03) | `js/physics.js` (e883a004) | decision: a hole made while the world is Static (a merger or collapse product, a hole the user places) moves until 50 units of simulated time have been integrated since it was made, then holds still; an Orbiting world always moves. 50 is 10 s times 5 units per second, which is `frameAdvance` at sim_speed 1 (50 * DT, DT = 0.1): what the wall-clock window came to on a machine drawing 20 frames a second or more at the sandbox's own speed. Why this length: it keeps the sandbox, where holes are placed at 1x, as it was, and it is a fixed length of simulated time, not scaled by playback speed, because the engine does not know the playback speed and must not (the answer would then depend on a control, not on the model). Consequences, stated: (1) the window no longer runs while the simulation is paused, so a hole placed during a pause moves for its 50 units once play resumes, where the wall clock had often used the window up; (2) a world that plays at a high sim_speed (scenarios with sim_speed in the hundreds) crosses 50 units in a fraction of a second of play, so a new hole there freezes almost at once, where it had drifted for 10 real seconds; (3) a backward step gives the window back, so a reversed run retraces the forward one. The window is counted per hole in the steps taken (a non-enumerable `graceUsed`, advanced where the hole's step is applied), not stamped on the clock: a restore builds every hole as new and then sets the clock to the saved one (`js/world.js` `applyShareState`), and a stamp would have been measured from the clock as it was before that write, stretching or erasing the window when the saved clock was earlier or later, or after `resetSimulationTime`. `tests/blackHoleCanMoveRestore.test.js` holds those three cases. Not changed: `creationTime` stays on the hole as a wall-clock stamp nothing reads, and `movementGracePeriod` stays 10 (seconds of play at 1x), so the serialized hole in the scenario goldens is byte-identical; `graceUsed` is not an own enumerable key for the same reason. Removing the dead stamp and storing the window in simulated units is a follow-up that moves `tests/fixtures/scenarioGeometryGolden.json` (7 rows) and 13 hashes in `tests/scenarioGeometry.test.js`, and is Carl's to approve. Evidence: `tests/blackHoleCanMove.test.js` drives one world on a 60 fps and a 15 fps machine: before, at 45 simulated units the 60 fps hole could move (9.0 s) and the 15 fps one could not (12.0 s), having stopped at x = 37.25 against 45; after, both can move at 45, both are static at 70, and they stop within one frame's advance of each other. | **RATIFIED** | Decided on the recommendation under Carl's ratification of D-R7-03 (2026-10-14, "Go with your recommendation on all"); the chosen length is the implementer's, pending Carl's review; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-15 (all decisions then waiting on him; "For each of those decisions that your are waiting for me on,  go with your best recommendation as my decision"; the recommendation is the decision) | Carl choosing a length scaled by playback speed (the engine would need sim_speed), or keeping the wall-clock window. | 113  |

So the builders stay in `js/physics.js` (verbatim, comments trimmed as before): the stream is then the same in every realm by construction, not by import discipline, and a new Worker or script that never imports `js/bodyEffects.js` cannot fork it. | D-DECOMP-18 | Prompt 107 step 2b, slice 5: the thirteen particle bursts become one table and one helper with every draw kept in the engine, their looks and the disk tracer's color table move to `js/bodyEffects.js`, and the engine/ split is designed (P107) | `js/physics.js` (a89e7a4b) | PART A, what moved. The thirteen bursts (a black hole absorbing a body, a disk tracer falling in, a star merger, a star swallowing a planet, a gas giant or an asteroid, a rocky collision, the three collapses, a gas giant's impact plume, a gas giant merger and its ignition) were thirteen loops of about twenty lines. They are now `BURSTS` (count, speed and lifetime) and `burst(name, pos, color, aim)` in `js/physics.js`: per particle one draw for the direction, one for the speed, then one for the lifetime, in the old order and with the old expressions (`Math.random() * range + floor`); a plume draws its direction around an aim, and a null color draws the first two and spawns nothing, which is what the absorption burst always did when a body's color was not a hex string (the color is worked out once before the loop, no draw depends on it). Count, speed and lifetime are random draws, so by D-DECOMP-16 they cannot leave the engine; what a burst looks like can. `burstLooks` (start size, end size, color of each burst) and `tracerColor(o)` (was `AccretionDiskParticle.getTemperatureColor`, 33 lines, read by its drawer and by the engine's own absorption burst) are in `js/bodyEffects.js` and filed with the engine by `registerEffects({ pool, looks, tracer })`, in the same module as the pool, so any realm with a pool has the colors and a realm without one has an empty look that nothing reads. `js/physics.js` 6,763 to 6,594 lines (ceiling lowered with `--record-sizes`), and the module ceilings are all exact so nothing could grow: `js/bodyEffects.js` took the 70 added lines by trimming the double-tap recognizer's history and per-method comments (343 to 341, ceiling lowered by 2), `js/bodyDrawSky.js` changed one import line, and no ceiling rose. NOT MOVED, with reasons. (1) The four explosion builders and their palettes: their sizes, lifetimes, glow and the color index are draws interleaved with the data, and the palette length is part of the index draw; a table would need the engine to hold each palette's length, which was judged more coupling than 26 lines of data were worth under a module ceiling that cannot take them. (2) The absorption burst's color gate: whether a body's base color is a hex string decides whether the lifetime is drawn, so that test stays beside the draws. (3) The gas giant's ring state (D-DECOMP-15, state). (4) The display glue (`DRAW_MIN_RADIUS_PX`, `liveBodyCount`, the four-radii note, about 30 lines): re-pointing `js/render.js` at `js/bodyVisuals.js` costs it four lines under an exact ceiling, for six lines out of the engine; left. (5) View code and picking (about 190 lines): `js/ui.js`, which this slice may not edit, imports `screen_to_world`, `findObjectAtPosition`, `resetTrailTick` and `SPACE_OBJECT_NAMES` from the engine, and the engine must not import the render layer to re-export them; `is_offscreen` is not appearance at all, it culls bodies off the canvas inside `updatePhysics` (11 call sites), so the engine's result depends on the page's canvas size and camera zoom (a zero-size canvas, which a Worker has, culls nothing). They move after the `js/ui.js` decomposition closes or through Part B's viewport seam. (6) Trails (the reference frame reads them) and names (`getRandomName` draws) stay. Seeded realm test (`tests/effectsRealm.test.js`) unchanged and green. PART B, design of the engine/ split (no code). AUDIT. `js/physics.js` has 6,594 lines, about 120 exports, 49 importers in `js/` (50 test files, 53 e2e specs, 20 tools; two Worker bundles carry the whole engine, the experiment runner and the validation Worker; the Barnes-Hut worker carries none), and 67 mutable module bindings: 62 `let` (14 body lists that `updatePhysics` and the mergers REASSIGN about 30 times, so importers hold live bindings and a test that captures one clears a detached copy; the settings object, replaced by a spread in `updatePhysicsSettings`; the camera/frame reference, the clocks and counters (`simulationTime`, `PhysicsObject_id_counter`, `worldGeneration`, `interventionEpoch`), `detailScale`, `trailTick`, `liveBodyCount`; seven Barnes-Hut worker variables; seven conservation and absorption accounting variables; fourteen integrator scratch Float64Arrays; six gravity cache variables; the collision grid; the pool, looks and tracer registrations) and 5 mutable containers (the drawers table, the step listeners, the barycenter cache, the grid buckets, the energy history). Sixteen exports have no importer in any source, test, spec or tool (the energy functions, `getAllPhysicsObjects`, two radius constants, `gwaves`, `handle_star_object_collisions` and others) and can be unexported in the slice that moves their code. What is not pure or Worker-safe today: `canvas` and `is_offscreen` (culling by the page's canvas and zoom, 11 sites), three `window` event dispatches (`dispatchSimulationEvent`, `gravitasMerge`, `gravitasWorkerFailed`) already behind `typeof` guards, wall-clock reads that reach the result (`BlackHole.can_move` compares `Date.now()` with the hole's creation time for a ten second grace period, so a newly made static hole moves for ten real seconds, which is a real nondeterminism that a headless fast-forward does not share; the ripples' `time` and `created` stamps feed only the renderer) and the Worker client. REGIONS (lines now): constants and units 140, state and settings and registries 500, events 40, conservation and absorption accounting 420 (accounting 100), energy history 470, force sources and caches 400, integrators 355, `updatePhysics` 740 (of which the Barnes-Hut worker dispatch is 150), the classes 1,575 (black hole and tracer 575, picking 140), collision grid 180, explosion builders and bursts 330, mergers and collapse and accretion 780, exports 130. PROPOSED SLICES, each behind `js/physics.js` kept as the one facade that re-exports (`export { x } from` keeps live bindings), so no importer and nothing in `js/ui.js` changes until the last slice: S1 `state` (the 14 lists with setters replacing the 30 reassignments, the settings and their update, the clocks and counters, the camera reference, the registries; about 330 lines; risk: a reassignment site missed, or an importer's live binding detached; proved by `e2e/worldConstruction.spec.js`, the world golden, `tests/update-physics.test.js`, a new facade test that pins the export list and that an importer's `planets` is the engine's after a step, `validate:physics` identical, `tools/seeded-step.mjs`); S2 `events` (the dispatches behind one sink the page registers, a Worker leaves empty; 90 lines; `tests/effectsRealm.test.js`, the merger e2e, the `gravitasMerge` listeners in the e2e specs); S3 `conservation` and `energy` (read-only over S1; 900 lines; the conservation tests, `validate:physics` conservation checks, the energy tab e2e); S4 `forces` and `integrator` (755 lines, the numerically sensitive pair, moved verbatim; `validate:physics` 304 of 304 identical, gravity assist, binary planets, black hole e2e, and `npm run perf` because a call now crosses a module); S5 `bodies` (classes without the black hole, two files under 1,500; `kind` accessor, saved states, `e2e/scenarioContract.spec.js`, `bodyPlacement`) and `blackHole` (black hole, tracer, absorption); S6 `collisions` (grid, rocky, gas giants, bursts) and `mergers` (the four builders, star merging, collapse): the RNG-order slices, proved by `effects-trace`, `effectsMissing`, `effectsRealm` and the 304; S7 `step` (`updatePhysics`) and `host` (the Barnes-Hut worker client, `clearCachedGravity`, the sink) with the viewport seam: a `setViewport(fn)` the page registers with the current culling rule, so a Worker, which registers nothing, culls nothing exactly as its zero-size canvas does today; proved by the Barnes-Hut e2e, the dist suite and the Worker bundles. Then a rule in `check:architecture` that the engine folder names no `document`, `window`, `localStorage` or `CustomEvent`, and the facade's importers migrate with the next feature that touches them. THE FIRST SLICE SHOULD BE S1, because every other piece reads the settings, the lists or the clocks and cannot leave `js/physics.js` without a cycle until they have a home; it is mechanical, it moves no number, and it is the seam the one-settings-truth work (step 2c, D-DECOMP-14) and any future multi-world need. RISKS. (a) Requests: the sources routes load one file per module and sit on their request ceilings (figure 117 of 117), so about ten new files are ten requests on every route that loads the engine; the standing rule that no request ceiling rises means either a fold of one-importer modules per slice (few remain on the figure route) or a decision by Carl before S2 on how the sources routes count an engine folder (the shipped build bundles it, and its request counts were unchanged by the earlier slices). (b) The bundler groups lazy chunks by entry set, so each slice must be measured on the build routes and may need re-exports, as slice 3 did. (c) `new Worker(new URL('./physicsWorker.js', import.meta.url))` resolves against the bundle in the build and the module in the sources, so the client must keep that spelling or move with the worker file; the dist suite and a Barnes-Hut run in the build prove it. (d) `tools/build-irreversibility-audit.mjs` and the docs facts cite `js/physics.js` lines, so each slice runs `audit:irreversible` and `docs:sync`. (e) The wall-clock grace period is a model behavior: replacing it with simulation time is a scientific decision, not part of any slice, and is recorded here for Carl. (f) Every module over 1,500 lines sits exactly at its ceiling, so a slice lowers `js/physics.js`'s in the same commit and the new files have no entry (1,500 limit). | **RATIFIED** | Decided under Carl's 2026-10-13 delegation of Prompt 107 decisions; the burst draws stay in the engine by D-DECOMP-16 and the merge queue's finding; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-14 (all delegated rows; "Go with your recommendation on all", his "Fo" corrected by his follow-up "Go*") | A reviewer wanting the palettes or the builders out of the engine (the engine would hold each palette's length), the burst table reading as too much engine, a decision by Carl on how the sources routes count an engine folder, or the wall-clock grace period replaced | 107 |

(1) axe 4.14 counts opacity: the gallery chip count measured 4.37:1 and the filled chip 4.23:1, so `.sc-chip-count` goes to opacity 0.85 and 1 on the filled chip (css/components.css); the contrast is a correction, not a theme change. (2) Chromium 156 re-fetches a module whose first fetch failed, so the in-page retry in e2e/deferredLocale.spec.js now resolves; the spec accepts either outcome and checks the strings when it resolves, because the application's answer (strings fall back, a reload recovers) is the same. (3, added 2026-10-17 after the queue's review) the in-page scroll plus mouse click skips Playwright's stability wait, so the specs now also assert the card's box is identical over two animation frames; on macOS WebKit the card sits about 6,900 px down the list, its box is constant over 30 frames and nothing animates on it, so the Linux stall's cause is NOT established, and if the card really loops on Linux that assertion fails there rather than passing. The two WebKit specs that timed out on CI's Linux WebKit (investigations.spec.js, stellarLesson.spec.js) pass on Mac WebKit 2370 and did not reproduce on the Mac but did on CI (3 specs, traces read): on Linux WebKit 1.64 the click on a card far down the list never reached "stable" when click() did its own scroll first, so the two helpers now call scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() before the click, and a third spec (startupLifecycle, a reload right after the splash) is made to wait for the page to finish loading so WebKit's abort-time console error ("home.html due to access control checks") does not count. If CI still times out the group stays held. (1) The corpus (tests/compat/: 18 record kinds, a matrix of old-reads-old, new-reads-old, what the 2.0.0 reader says of the current writer and so of a rollback or an old cache, a round trip, capabilities and an unknown-field probe, run against the v2.0.0 commit's own readers) is green; no writer or reader changed. (2) The policy (FORMATS.md, INTEGRATION.md): a writer changes only when its row is green for the change; a change that makes an older build refuse or silently misread is a major-version boundary on the 3.0 train (176); where a payload needs no new fields the writer writes the old version; a record a new reader needs that an old one would ignore is a capability-required refusal, never an unknown field. The support period is PROPOSED: never withdrawn within a major version; after a superseding major version, 12 months deprecated (read and written), 12 months read-only, then retired with an export path, announced in CHANGELOG one release ahead. (3) Measured: 2.0.0's pack and manifest readers (course packs, investigation pack, capability package) refuse an unknown field; its envelope and record readers (artifact, observation, experiment, progress records, results, ledger) accept it and drop it silently. (1) THE VERSION: `gravitas.artifact` stays at 1. The corpus row (`not-constrained-state`) says a 2.0.0 reader refuses a quantity whose uncertainty kind it does not know, in its own words, and drops `fit` and `correlatedWith` without a word; the second is acceptable because no reader needs either, and the first is safe because it is a capability-required refusal. So the writers keep their 2.0.0 output by default (`fitArtifact` gains an `extended` option and writes the new states and the record only when asked), and `legacyView()` gives a 2.0.0 reader the envelope it can open: each refused state becomes `none`, `fit` and `correlatedWith` are left out, a failed quantity (which has no value) is left out, and each loss is listed in the warnings as `extended:<id>:<kind>`. The way back is exact for the three 2.0.0 kinds and for them alone, which `tests/uncertaintyContract.test.js` holds on every kind and basis. Version 2 waits for Prompt 176. (2) THE STATES: `not-constrained` (the data leave the value open), `failed` (no result; `reason`, and a `null` value), `assumed` (taken as exact, which is not the unknown that `none` is), `model-limited` (a model error `floor` bounds the precision), `limit` (a nondetection: an `upper` or `lower` bound, with `level`). The asymmetric interval already existed as `lo` and `hi`; it gains a validated `level` on every kind that has one, and the sides are read from the value. The state names follow the compatibility fixtures of Prompt 134, not a new spelling. (3) THE FIT: the fit's result record (model and version, parameters by quantity id, the covariance in a stated order with each parameter's registry unit, the statistic and degrees of freedom, residual count and rms, the rows' digest, algorithm, settings and seed (null: the grid and the refinement are deterministic), convergence, rank) is built by `fitRecord` beside `fitArtifact`; no second representation was made. `js/inference/fit.js` gains `rankAt`: the information matrix is scaled to unit diagonal, its eigenvalues are read against the largest, and a parameter with at least 1% of its weight in a direction below 1e-8 of it, or one the model does not use, is not constrained. `infer.js` writes the result as `results.fit.rank`, flags the parameters, and warns `notConstrained`, in both languages; no fitted value and no sigma changed. The tolerance and the 1% are stated choices, not tuned to a case. (4) THE FORMULA: `evaluate` takes `assumed` (exact); `evaluateStates` in `js/formula/evidence.js` takes `model-limited` (its floor propagates) and one `limit`, and refuses `not-constrained`, `failed`, `interval` and a bare `limit` in words in both languages. A limit passes through a formula that rises or falls steadily from a quarter of it to the whole, checked at four points, not proved, with the other inputs exact: the result is a limit with the bound flipped if the formula falls. It lives beside the derivation record so the language stays under its byte ceiling (engine 5,932 of 6,144 gzipped; grader 6,374 of 6,656). (5) THE TEXT: `formatUncertain` writes a quantity at the precision its uncertainty sets (a sigma, or a symmetric interval's half-width; the smaller side of an asymmetric one; a limit as "<" or ">"; a model floor as the sigma) and says which method it used on request; `parseUncertain` reads a typed uncertainty ("±", "+/-", "9.81(2)", "+0.05 -0.03", "<", ">") through the shared number reader, handed in so the module stays a leaf. Both live in `js/platform/uncertain.js`, not in `js/format.js`, which is a source of the instructor bundle (a change to it needs the passphrase rebuild); nothing imports the new module yet, so no route pays for it until Prompt 151 adopts it. A sigma or a symmetric interval prints "X ± Y" at the uncertainty's precision (two figures of Y), an asymmetric interval "X +U −L", a limit "< X" or "> X", a failed quantity the words "no result", a quantity the data leave open "not constrained", each followed by one word in brackets for where the uncertainty came from: data, model, rescaled (the data uncertainty scaled by the fit's quality), profile, propagated (to first order from the inputs'), stated, limit, exact. The word is the envelope's `basis` (`assumed` is said "stated", `derived` "propagated", `scaled` "rescaled"); a model-limited value is "model"; a quantity that states no uncertainty is printed with no word and no change. The word carries its one-sentence meaning as a title on the notebook page (focusable) and the glossary page has an entry for each. WHERE. The notebook entry's table, the PDF report's table (and so the HTML export, which writes the same document) and the evidence ledger's table, through one helper (`quantityText` for a notebook quantity, `rowValue` for a ledger row). The variance gains the cross terms 2 rho gj gk sj sk on the gradient the engine already carries, so a quantity used twice is still differentiated once; the result reports `info.correlated` and the derivation's rule is `first-order-correlated` (`first-order-uncorrelated` otherwise, which the preview words as independent inputs), and the derivation records the coefficients used by input id and puts them in the source digest only when there are some, so every existing derivation keeps its digest. The engine trusts what it is given; `checkCorrelations` in `js/formula/evidence.js` (each coefficient within -1 to 1, between two different inputs, one value per pair, and the set a correlation matrix by Cholesky) is the check that `derivedEntry` and the panel's preview make first, and a refusal is `formula.err.correlation`, in both languages. It is in `evidence.js` because the language's byte ceilings (engine 6,144 and grader 6,656 gzipped, D-FORMULA-01) leave little room, and CI gzips under Node 20, about 73 bytes larger than Node 24 does here: the engine measures 6,052 locally (about 6,125 on CI) and the grader 6,503. The engine adds only the cross terms, the pair lookup and the `correlated` flag, and a bad set of coefficients that skipped the check would give a NaN sigma, not a wrong number. | D-R10-09 | Prompt 151 part C (comparison): the comparison of two estimates of one quantity is a pure module, `js/compare/estimates.js`, that takes the covariance when it is known and says when it assumed independence; the instrument that calls it is not yet in the product, so nothing on a page imports it | `js/compare/estimates.js` (d7036c9f) | decision. The roadmap names an instrument's "compare two results"; the repository has the model-against-data comparison (`js/compare/compare.js`), which compares one model with one observation and has no second estimate to compare, and no instrument that compares two results. So this part builds the part that is not an instrument: `compareEstimates(a, b, {covariance, rho, shared})` gives the difference, its sigma from Var(A-B) = Var(A) + Var(B) - 2 Cov(A, B), the significance in sigma and the two-sided Gaussian tail probability, and the assumptions it rests on (`gaussian`, then `independent` or `covariance`, and `sharedUnknown` when the two are known to share data or calibration and nothing says how they move together, which is the louder caveat). The covariance may be stated, a coefficient, or the coefficient an envelope gives between two quantities of one fit (`correlationBetween`, from `correlatedWith`); a covariance larger than the two uncertainties allow is refused. Uncertainties it can use: a sigma, an exact assumed value, a model floor with its sigma, a symmetric interval with its confidence level; a limit, a failed or unconstrained quantity, an asymmetric interval or one with no level is refused in words that name which estimate. The tail uses an `erfc` held to published values on both sides of its switch. Words are `compareW.est.*` in the compare catalogs, both languages, registered where the family loads. Because no page imports the module, no route, bundle or deferred budget moves. The instrument that uses it (a side-by-side comparison of two notebook entries) is the later prompt that adds the surface; this is its tested core. | **RATIFIED** | Reviewed by Carl, 2026-11-12 (ratified on the ratification pack's recommendation; was DELEGATED: Proposed by Prompt 151 part C, 2026-10-18; delegated under Carl's standing instruction on non-scientific decisions) | Inventing the instrument's panel in this part (a new surface with its own accessibility, localization and budget work, which is a prompt of its own), or folding the function into `js/platform/uncertain.js` (it would then cost every notebook route its bytes) | 151 |

| D-R10-13 | Prompt 137 (engine validation debt): the Barnes-Hut tree, the collision-outcome table, every burst kind and a long-run regression are under the suite against tolerances committed first, two departures are characterized rather than conserved, the inspiral stays unvalidated by decision, and "What is not validated" is generated from `tools/validation-gaps.json` and read by the model page | `js/validation/engineTolerances.js` (434e2d7c) | decision, with findings for Carl. **Tolerances** were committed before any check ran, each with its literature (Barnes and Hut 1986, Hernquist 1987, Salmon and Warren 1994, Springel 2005); no tolerance was changed after a measurement. **Barnes-Hut at theta 0.4** on three seeded worlds (cluster, two clumps, a disc about a heavy centre): mean force error 0.44 percent against 1, worst single body 9.2 percent against a bound of 10 (close to its bound: a finding to watch, not to widen), net force 0.14 percent of the force magnitudes against 1, and tree-driven energy drift 0.098 percent against 1 with the direct-sum difference 0.038 percent. The first read of the energy drift was 1.9 percent, a failure of the harness, not of the tree: it summed energy with a hard distance clamp that the force is not the gradient of, and the direct-sum run drifted the same; the potential was made the one the clamped force derives from and the one-percent tolerance was not touched. **Outcome table**: 12 canonical merger pairs and 6 collapse cases give the documented products, and mass and momentum are exact (1e-12) for every merger, collapse, gas-giant accretion and gas-giant merger (through-the-step 1e-9 for the star-forming gas merger); all 13 bursts alter no body. **Two departures found and characterized, not changed (a finding for the register, the tolerance stays):** (1) a star that absorbs a planet, gas giant or asteroid adds the mass and keeps its own velocity, so the system loses m(v_body - v_star) of momentum (the black-hole path conserves it; the star path does not); (2) a rocky collision above a relative speed of 15 multiplies each body's mass by 0.9 and throws floor(speed/8)+2 fragments of a tiny fixed mass, so a tenth of the pair's mass leaves the system. Fixing either is a model change and Carl's call. **Regression**: the first sample tried (random bound systems at a virial ratio of one quarter) had a median drift of 1,900 percent, collapse and encounter dominated, and was dropped as an unusable instrument; the recorded sample is 50 seeds of a perturbed Lagrange triangle, 1,000 steps of 0.05, median 0.61 percent and 90th percentile 48 percent, bounds 1.25 times those (a 1e-13 change in the initial positions moves neither). It validates no physical statistic. **The inspiral** stays unvalidated against general relativity, as the roadmap decides: the suite checks the code against the model page's stated decay and measures the departure. | **RATIFIED** | Reviewed by Carl, 2026-11-12 (ratified on the ratification pack's recommendation; was DELEGATED: Proposed by Prompt 137, 2026-10-19; delegated under Carl's standing instruction on non-scientific decisions; the two departures, the regression sample and the inspiral decision are not yet reviewed by Carl) | Widening a tolerance to pass (refused by the prompt); fixing the two departures in this prompt (a model change); validating the tree through a Worker shim | 137 |

| D-R10-228-08 | The fix for D-R10-228-07, a lesson panel that mounts or opens late escaping a modal. Cause, found by opening a lesson over each kind of modal: the lesson's markup is a fragment mounted (`js/i18n/dom.js` `mountFragment`) the first time a lesson opens, as new children of `<body>` after `js/dialog.js` `isolate()` had walked them once, so with an isolating dialog (the scenario gallery, the lecture sequence, the corrupt-state notice) the panel, plot, ellipse and tool docks came in live and focusable; and `openInvestigation` then called `els.title.focus()` unconditionally, which took focus out of any open modal, the non-isolating precise-placement form and Settings included (that is how Tab from the mass field reached `investigationClose`). Fix, two lines of behaviour: `isolate()` watches `<body>` with a MutationObserver while its dialog is open and makes a late arrival inert, with the same rules as the first walk (live regions and already-inert nodes left alone) and releases it, and the observer, on close; `openInvestigation` moves focus to the lesson title only when focus is not inside an `aria-modal="true"` element. Scope kept minimal: no change to precise placement's deliberate lack of a scrim, and the two specs' preconditions from 522c9c56 are left as they are. Regression tests: `tests/dialogBackdrop.test.js` (four, the first fails without the fix) and two in `e2e/accessibilityParity.spec.js` that open a lesson over the precise-placement form and over the gallery (both fail on v3 20c9ab0b, both pass with the fix). | D-R10-285-02 | Prompt 285, **reduced computation modes**. `computation` in `tools/perf-thresholds.json` is the one table of the sizes each tier computes at (bootstrap draws 1000 and 300, Monte Carlo draws 20,000 and 5000, profile points 11 and 7, worker realms 8 and 2, worker bytes 1 GB and 256 MB); `js/quality.js` mirrors it (a static page cannot read `tools/`) and `tests/computeTier.test.js` holds the two equal and holds every key to the one file that reads it. Kernels take sizes as arguments and never read the tier, so they give the same numbers at both tiers for the same argument; the caller asks for the size. Tolerances were written into the file before the validators ran: bootstrap standard error within 15 percent (measured worst 8.6 percent over 12 seeds), mass-sum interval ends within 3 percent of the width (measured worst 2.7 percent, near the line: 5000 is the least that passes, not a comfortable figure), profile ends within 5 percent of the half-width (measured 3.3 percent). The worker caps change no number. A smaller drawn frame for the low tier was NOT adopted: the image marks module's size gate (25,600 B in `tests/imageMeasureBudget.test.js`, a measured gate this session may not raise) leaves no room for the tier's import. A result computed at the low tier says so: the fit panel's line and button ("Compute at the full tier"), the exported document's `computation`, and the envelope's `provenance.computation`, which is absent at the full tier so a full-tier envelope is unchanged; the ensemble record states its `draws` and the orbit tool's `method` string its count. Not adopted, recommendation: the mission lab's porkchop grid and the visual-binary and orbit-fit Monte Carlos with fixed counts, because the mission page has no classifier and those counts are named in tested method strings; a follow-up can take each with its own tolerance. | `js/quality.js` (b4ac1b70) | decision, numerics | **RATIFIED** | Reviewed by Carl, 2026-11-12 (ratified on the ratification pack's recommendation; was DELEGATED: Proposed by Prompt 285, 2026-11-11; no scientific gate involved (no kernel's numbers change for a given argument)) | Carl wanting a different low size for a key, which is a one-line change in two files that the test keeps equal | 285 |
| D-R10-285-03 | Prompt 285, **the classifier on pages that never render the simulation**: the classifier is fed only by the simulation's render loop, so the Observatory, the 3-D lab and reports never decide (`qualityReport().decided` is false) and compute at the full tier unless `?quality=low` or `?quality=full` is in the address (`applyTierRequest`, nothing stored). Found, not fixed: an idle page's frame rate says nothing about the machine, so a frame classifier there would be a guess, and carrying the simulation page's verdict across pages needs a registered storage key. Recommendation: a sessionStorage key for the verdict (one decision, STORAGE.md and the key registry), as its own small PR; until then a student on a slow machine who opens the Observatory first gets full-size computation and the button state is the full tier's. Thresholds (32 and 48 fps) are unchanged: on the heaviest scene the classifier decides at all three profiles (10.0, 4.6 and 7.5 fps at the full tier, all demoted). Covered by tests: a page with no frames reports `decided: false` and computes at the full tier; frames inside the warm-up decide nothing; a 150 fps machine is still judged; reset forgets the verdict. | `js/quality.js` (b4ac1b70) | decision, open question | **RATIFIED** | Reviewed by Carl, 2026-11-12 (ratified on the ratification pack's recommendation; was DELEGATED: Proposed by Prompt 285, 2026-11-11; for Carl: the recommendation above) | Carl choosing the storage key now | 285 |
| D-R10-285-04 | Prompt 285, **automated device profiles**: `e2e/deviceProfiles.spec.js` runs five workflows (start, a lesson step, an image mark, a fit, a 3-D run) under three profiles in `tools/perf-thresholds.json` `deviceProfiles` (the throttled desktop CPU 4x as it has been run here; a low-end laptop CPU 6x, 10 Mbps and 40 ms, 512 MB heap ceiling, low tier; a mid-range phone 412 x 915 at 2.625, touch, CPU 6x, 1.6 Mbps and 150 ms, 384 MB heap ceiling, low tier), each a Chromium launched with `--js-flags=--max-old-space-size` (a project option cannot do that per profile) and throttled over the DevTools protocol. The spec runs in the ordinary e2e shards (`.github` is not edited; no workflow names the thresholds file, which `tests/perfTrace.test.js` requires). Time budgets are three times the measured value, rounded up to 100 ms and at least 4 s; heap budgets twice the measured used heap after a forced collection, at least 8 MB: a shared runner has its own load and a repeated local run varied by a factor of two. They are PROXIES: the CPU throttle slows the main thread only (the fit and the 3-D run are Workers), the heap flag bounds JavaScript memory and not decoded images or the GPU, the network shape is a rate and a delay. The real-device profiles stay empty and the `low-end-profiles` claim in `tools/evidence-status.json` is UNKNOWN. CI is the gate for the budgets: a budget it fails is raised only to a new measurement with its own row, never to pass. The lesson step on the phone profile takes 82 s to usable (the network and code size at 1.6 Mbps and CPU 6x), the largest figure and a finding for the lesson route's weight. | `e2e/deviceProfiles.spec.js` (b4ac1b70) | decision, test | **RATIFIED** | Reviewed by Carl, 2026-11-12 (ratified on the ratification pack's recommendation; was DELEGATED: Proposed by Prompt 285, 2026-11-11; the budgets are new, none is loosened) | Carl wanting tighter budgets once CI has timed them | 285 |
